Two false measurements were caught while building it: the first run credited the machine with the instrument's own injected bug because git status reported it as an edit, and the first injection broke 644 of 1014 click tests, which is a demolition rather than a bug report.

evidence: Measured: a cold discovery of the same one-action goal costs 7,147 ms; the recalled answer costs 670 ms. Deleting the memory is correct and ten times slower, which makes it a non-answer to a question about SPEED.
qualification_evidence: direct probe: cenv.discover('compress notes.txt into notes.txt.bz2') cold 7,147 ms, recalled 670 ms, this session

evidence: A machine-level cache makes two goals on the SAME machine agree, which is half the defect. It does nothing for the other half: installing one program changes the cache key, so the next fingerprint is compared against a remembered one by the same equality test and scores 0.0 again. It treats the symptom (probe cost) and not the gate.
qualification_evidence: direct probe: with one extra binary on PATH the action set changes, so any cache keyed by the program set is a miss on exactly the machine change that erased the memory

evidence: Measured and honest: a plain Jaccard score with the floor moved from 0.5 to 0.35 reproduces all four cases this change needs -- 0.400 for a narrow sample of the same machine, 0.976 for one extra program, 0.000 for a different kind of environment. It is defeated on a different axis: 0.35 is a constant that encodes the CURRENT shortlist sizes (14 programs for '.gz', 40 for a wider goal), so adding a goal with a two-program shortlist makes it wrong again with nothing to notice. Overlap asks the question that stays true -- 'is the smaller sample contained in the larger one' -- and needs no constant.
qualification_evidence: direct probe: Jaccard 0.400 / 0.976 / 0.000 measured this session; shortlists observed at 14 and 40 actions for two different goals

evidence: A fingerprint is a SAMPLE of the machine's vocabulary, so the similarity question is containment, not equality. The guard that no plan is believed without execution is unchanged, which is what makes a generous gate safe: a wrong recall costs one trial, a zero recall costs every trial forever. replayable() closes the one new risk -- a plan naming a program this machine lacks -- and it is filtered rather than tried and recorded as disproven.
qualification_evidence: direct probe: 7,147 ms cold -> 670 ms same machine -> 699 ms with a changed program inventory; 58 tests pass; unified model 33/33

stop_condition: STOP when a real repository with an injected bug is repaired by an edit the machine produced and the project's own suite goes green without the operator touching the code.
weakens_existing_guard: Nothing is weakened. The instrument is stricter than the census: the oracle is a third party's suite rather than a check written alongside the sentence, the bug is not authored by the same hand as the fix, and a dirty tree can no longer be read as the machine's work because the injection is committed before the first attempt.
